subject: Post-demo: ParcelPro cost targets & model allocation
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@parcelpro.ai>, Chris Duarte <chris@parcelpro.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: ParcelPro cost targets & model allocation

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation, Olivia + Chris. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on pricing/volume before we move to a follow-up with procurement.

Recap (what we heard)
- Monthly active queries: ~3M end-user queries/month (peak daily ~150k).
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens in + 220 tokens out (avg 340 tokens total).
- Primary use cases: conversational chat (customer support triage), embeddings for semantic search (product catalog), and a small rerank flow for top-10 results.
- Data residency: US only; privacy-sensitive PII redaction required.

Our initial ask to you: please confirm the rough monthly token estimate we used below so we can firm up the unit pricing.

Proposed token and model mix (for pricing exercise) — please confirm if this matches your expectations:
- Total monthly tokens (estimate): 3M queries * 340 tokens = ~1.02B tokens/month.
- Allocation by service:
  - Chat (primary): 70% -> ~714M tokens/month
  - Embeddings (batch indexing + realtime similarity): 25% -> ~255M tokens/month
  - Rerank (inference on top candidates, smaller prompts): 5% -> ~51M tokens/month

Target unit economics we want to qualify for procurement: what price band do you need for a committed tier?
- Pilot (90 days) target: $900–1,200 per 1M tokens (chat-weighted effective)
- Committed annual target: $600–850 per 1M tokens depending on model mix & SLA

Notes on model mix & options we can recommend:
- Chat: recommend a medium-latency conversational model (Redwood-curated 13B variant) for most traffic; we can route tail requests to a lower-cost 7B for cheaper or to a higher-quality 70B for escalation.
- Embeddings: use compact embeddings for dot-product similarity; we can shard heavy indexing to a batch-optimized node pool to reduce unit cost.
- Rerank: small cross-encoder calls — expensive per token but small volume. Consider caching rerank outputs for repeated queries.

Attachments: I attached a simple workbook that maps these numbers to a 3-tier pricing sketch and a CSV with the baseline unit-econ assumptions.

Next steps / asks
1) Please confirm the monthly query and token assumptions (3M queries, ~1.02B tokens) or send your corrected numbers.
2) Tell us which unit price band is realistic for you for a 90-day pilot vs. annual commit.
3) If OK, we’ll prepare a short SOW for a 90-day pilot with a stepped pricing ladder and predefined roll criteria.

If helpful, Marissa can join procurement calls next week. Proposed internal owners below.

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-03-15T18:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ParcelPro cost targets & model allocation

Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns broadly with what we captured; a few clarifications and one request: 

Confirmations / clarifications:
- Monthly queries: our product analytics show 2.7–3.2M queries depending on promotional spikes — 3M is fine as a baseline.
- Token avg: we reviewed several sessions and 340 tokens total is a good working assumption.

One ask on model mix: we expect embeddings traffic to grow faster as we onboard more SKUs and do more semantic search. Can you show pricing buckets with a 35% embeddings case (instead of 25%) so we can see impact?

On pricing: procurement wants to see a pilot price at or under $1,100 per 1M effective tokens and an annual committed band no higher than $800 per 1M. They also asked whether there are blended discounts if we commit by SKU (embeddings-heavy).

Also — curious about fallback behavior: if your dedicated pool is saturated during peaks, what are the routes and cost implications? Can someone on your team share a short note?

Happy to jump on a quick call Thursday to go over specifics; I cc’ed Chris who owns procurement.

Best,
Olivia

--

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@parcelpro.ai>, Chris Duarte <chris@parcelpro.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ParcelPro cost targets & model allocation

Thanks, Olivia — great questions. Short answers below and then an updated plan attached.

Regarding the embeddings-heavy scenario
- We re-ran the quick sketch with 35% embeddings (keeping total tokens constant at 1.02B):
  - Chat: 60% -> ~612M tokens
  - Embeddings: 35% -> ~357M tokens
  - Rerank: 5% -> ~51M tokens
- That mix increases the effective compute per query in ways that can lower the blended chat unit price but increase embedding units; we show two blended price examples in the attached workbook (pilot & annual).

Pricing commitments & blended discounts
- Pilot: we can accept $1,100 / 1M tokens for the standard mix you signed off on; if you opt for the embeddings-heavy variant, we would structure a blended pilot rate at $1,050 / 1M with a 30% of-volume move to batch-indexing windows to reduce peak pressure.
- Annual: we can target $750 / 1M for a 12-month commit at the baseline mix. For embeddings-heavy commitments we can add a SKU-level discount (tiered by embeddings volume) that can bring effective price to ~$700 / 1M depending on the commit size.

Fallbacks and routing (short summary)
- Smart routing: we route requests by policy. If Dedicated pool is saturated we: (1) route to overflow nodes in a lower-cost pool (slightly higher latency), (2) apply graceful degradation rules — favor LLM-lite models for non-critical queries, and (3) temporarily queue batch-eligible embeddings into a batch-index window to avoid direct compute.
- Cost implication: overflow routing can change unit price by +10–25% depending on model variant; we’ll include an expected range in the workbook.

Proposed next steps
1) Hannah/Vivek to deliver updated workbook showing both 25% and 35% embeddings mixes + pilot vs annual blended prices (attached). (Owner: Hannah)
2) Procurement sync with Marissa + Olivia to confirm SOW acceptance and payment/PO cadence. (Owner: Marissa)
3) Tech deep-dive to review fallbacks and SLA behaviors (Owner: Vivek) — propose Tue 03/21 10:00am PT for a 30-minute session.

If that schedule works, Marissa will send a calendar invite and we’ll draft a simple 90-day pilot SOW with the price ladder.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Hannah
